package_info.why_malicious: This report is a best practices guide and does not describe any specific malicious package. It discusses common attack vectors (repository hijacking, typosquatting, dependency confusion) but does not provide concrete examples or code snippets of malicious packages.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected package publication from hijacked maintainer accounts
Packages with names similar to popular projects (typosquatting)
Public packages overriding private/internal dependencies (dependency confusion)
file_indicators: Packages with names differing by a single character from popular packages
Unexpected new versions published by unknown or recently changed maintainers
network_indicators: Installer scripts reaching out to public repositories for dependencies that should be internal
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or unexpected package versions, especially from maintainers with recent account changes. Flag packages with names similar to popular ones. Detect installer scripts or build processes that resolve dependencies from public repositories when private/internal ones are expected. Use code review and signed releases to verify provenance and integrity.
